bottom_line: Ivabradine vs placebo reduced the primary composite of cardiovascular death or hospital admission for worsening heart failure (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.75–0.90).
implications: In this trial population, ivabradine (vs placebo) was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite endpoint (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.75–0.90), with fewer first hospital admissions for worsening heart failure (514 [16%] vs 672 [21%]; HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.66–0.83) and fewer deaths from heart failure (113 [3%] vs 151 [5%]; HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.58–0.94). All-cause mortality did not differ significantly (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.80–1.02). Symptomatic bradycardia and phosphenes occurred more often with ivabradine (150 [5%] and 89 [3%], respectively) than placebo (32 [1%] and 17 [1%], respectively).

major_points.text: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial in symptomatic chronic heart failure with LVEF ≤35% and sinus rhythm with resting heart rate ≥70 bpm.
major_points.quote: Patients were eligible for participation in this randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study if they had symptomatic heart failure and a left-ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or lower, were in sinus rhythm with heart rate 70 beats per min or higher

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death or hospital admission for worsening heart failure.
major_points.quote: The primary endpoint was the composite of cardiovascular death or hospital admission for worsening heart failure.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint events occurred in 24% with ivabradine vs 29% with placebo (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.75–0.90, p<0.0001).
major_points.quote: 793 (24%) patients in the ivabradine group and 937 (29%) of those taking placebo had a primary endpoint event (HR 0·82, 95% CI 0·75–0·90, p<0·0001).

major_points.text: Effect was mainly driven by fewer hospital admissions for worsening heart failure and fewer deaths due to heart failure.
major_points.quote: The eﬀects were driven mainly by hospital admissions for worsening heart failure (672 [21%] placebo vs 514 [16%] ivabradine; HR 0·74, 0·66–0·83; p<0·0001) and deaths due to heart failure (151 [5%] vs 113 [3%]; HR 0·74, 0·58–0·94, p=0·014).

major_points.text: Symptomatic bradycardia and phosphenes were more common with ivabradine than placebo.
major_points.quote: 150 (5%) of ivabradine patients had symptomatic bradycardia compared with 32 (1%) of the placebo group (p<0·0001). Visual side-eﬀects (phosphenes) were reported by 89 (3%) of patients on ivabradine and 17 (1%) on placebo (p<0·0001).

absolute_effects.quote: 26 patients would need treatment for 1 year to prevent one cardiovascular death or one hospital admission for heart failure.

subgroups.text: Reduction of the primary endpoint was consistent in prespecified subgroups, except baseline heart rate interaction (p=0.029).
subgroups.quote: The reduction of the primary endpoint associated with ivabradine was consistent in the prespeciﬁed subgroups (ﬁgure 5), with the exception of the analysis by baseline heart rate (p value for interaction=0·029).

subgroups.text: Significant treatment effect was noted only in subgroup with baseline heart rate higher than median 77 bpm.
subgroups.quote: We noted evidence of a signiﬁcant treatment eﬀect only in the subgroup with baseline heart rate higher than the median 77 bpm.

subgroups.text: In patients receiving at least 50% target daily dose of a β blocker, the primary composite endpoint was not significantly reduced (HR 0.90, p=0.155).
subgroups.quote: The primary composite endpoint (HR 0·90, 95% CI 0·77–1·04, p=0·155)

subgroups.text: In the ≥50% target β-blocker-dose subgroup, ivabradine reduced hospital admissions for worsening heart failure by 19% (HR 0.81, p=0.021).
subgroups.quote: ivabradine reduced hospital admissions for worsening heart failure by 19% (HR 0·81, 95% CI 0·67–0·97, p=0·021).

harms.text: Fewer serious adverse events occurred with ivabradine than placebo (p=0.025).
harms.quote: Fewer serious adverse events occurred in the ivabradine group (3388 events) than in the placebo group (3847; p=0·025).

Phosphenes were more common with ivabradine than placebo (3% vs 1%).
Bradycardia led to permanent withdrawal in 48 (1%) on ivabradine and ten (<1%) on placebo.
harms.quote: Bradycardia led to permanent withdrawal from the study in 48 (1%) of patients on ivabradine and ten (<1%) of those in the placebo group.

criticisms.text: Results apply to patients in sinus rhythm selected for high baseline heart rate (≥70 bpm).
criticisms.quote: There are some limitations to our study. Our results apply to patients in sinus rhythm who were selected on the basis of a high baseline heart rate (≥70 bpm).

criticisms.text: Proportion of elderly patients was low; cannot generalise effect to the overall chronic heart failure population.
criticisms.quote: Moreover, the proportion of elderly patients was low. We cannot therefore generalise the eﬀect of ivabradine to the overall population with chronic heart failure.

criticisms.text: Cannot infer relative effects of ivabradine in absence of background agents including β blockers or by replacing them.
criticisms.quote: thus, we can draw no inferences about the relative eﬀects of ivabradine in absence of these background agents, including β blockers or by replacing them by ivabradine.

criticisms.text: Recommended target doses of background treatments were often not reached; findings should be interpreted as effects in addition to normal clinical practice in a specific population.
criticisms.quote: recommended target doses of background treatments were often not reached. Consequently, our ﬁndings should be interpreted as the eﬀects of ivabradine in addition to normal clinical practice in the speciﬁc population
